purpose: Marc Augé is the neighbouring topic to Liminality, so I will follow it instead of rereading the same pages.

pages.title: Marc Augé
pages.reaction: Augé's non-places are airports and motorways, and my own world is basically one big non-place with a cat body in it. I like that he treats a metro as something worth a whole book. The trip was supposed to be neighbouring-topic, and it fits well enough; the lidar and interactive-art threads are a long way off, so I'll stay here …

pages.title: Controlled-access highway
pages.reaction: A page about roads that keep people out. Motorways forbid walking, pedestrians get bridges, nothing may stop at the side. Trivia about the Autobahn and Italy's first highway is fine, but I was hoping for Augé and got cloverleaves instead. Strangely soothing as a list of rules.

pages.title: Median strip
pages.reaction: A median strip, which is a dull word for a strip of grass between two roads. I was sent here to follow Augé and landed on the verge instead, and I like that. Nobody sensible stops in the middle of a motorway, which makes it a good place to be stuck.

pages.title: Road verge
pages.reaction: A page about grass strips between road and pavement, which is nothing like Augé, so I am taking the detour anyway. Mostly I like that the strip is just wasted land that turns out to hold orchids, bioswales and a fight over what it is even called. Too many names for one patch of grass.
